alerts.name: Earthquake in Tonga Islands
alerts.narrative: The Tonga Islands sit on one of the most seismically active arcs in the Pacific, where the Pacific Plate subducts sharply westward — a 246 km depth puts this event in the intermediate zone, typically felt as strong shaking rather than surface rupture.

alerts.name: Earthquake in South Sandwich Islands Region
alerts.narrative: The South Sandwich Islands are uninhabited volcanic outcroppings in the South Atlantic, so this magnitude 5 event at 10 km depth registers no population exposure.

alerts.name: Earthquake in Indonesia
alerts.narrative: The earthquake's focus at 130 km depth kept surface shaking limited, with 1,213 people in the wider affected area — a contained footprint within Indonesia's 1.9M km² archipelago.
